tagline: Seven hundred white poles, and an outlaw at either end.
intro: Out of Adair the old road runs east beside Interstate 80, 26 miles through Casey, Menlo and Stuart to Dexter, past some 700 telephone poles painted white. It began as a dirt road in the early 1900s and became Iowa's first certified route under the State Highway Commission.

Auto tourists of the day called it the Great White Way. In good weather you can leave the pavement for remnant stretches of the 1913 route, where the old railroad tracks ran alongside before the automobile got Iowa out of the mud.

moments.title: Adair
moments.text: A steam engine wheel marks where the Jesse James gang derailed the Rock Island Express in July 1873 and left with $3,000, the first successful train robbery in the American West.

moments.title: Stuart
moments.text: In Stuart the Saints Center for Culture and the Arts rose from an arson's ashes and now houses the Learning Museum of Religious Tolerance.

moments.title: Dexter
moments.text: The Barrow gang shot it out here with police from as far away as Des Moines in July 1933, and in 1948 President Truman spoke at the national plowing match.
